big_case_rationale: Decides whether dozens of pending municipal and state climate-tort suits seeking billions against energy producers can proceed under state law; the Term's opening and likely most consequential environmental-federalism case.

semantic_claims.proposition: The majority holds Boulder's Colorado-law claims precluded because interstate and international greenhouse-gas emissions are a field governed exclusively by federal law under Milwaukee I, Milwaukee II, Ouellette and AEP: the Clean Air Act displaced federal common law but preserved, through its saving clause as Ouellette construed the Clean Water Act's, only claims under the law of the source State, so the law of an affected State like Colorado cannot supply the rule of decision. It treats the deception/marketing framing as not altering the claims' gravamen (injury from global emissions), and does not rest on a freestanding constitutional extraterritoriality holding.

The holding is categorical rather than case-specific: it bars any suit applying an affected (non-source) State's law to seek redress for injuries from out-of-state and global greenhouse-gas emissions, reaching all similarly pleaded municipal and state climate suits regardless of the label (nuisance, trespass, deception) on the claims, while expressly leaving open whether a source-State-law suit against in-state emitters could proceed.
